The best personal sites remain usable after dozens of pieces, not just at launch. That usually depends less on visual novelty than on a stable editorial structure.

Treating content as an archive from the beginning changes the design choices you make. It pushes you toward small metadata systems, durable URLs, and distinctions between front-door work and everything else.

That is why the combination of `content_type`, `access`, and `tier` matters. It gives the site enough structure to stay legible without forcing every entry into a heavy publishing workflow.
